name: previous_day_hl_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY breaks above its previous session high on 5-second bars with a >2.5x volume surge (vs 5-minute rolling average), VWAP-benchmarked institutional algorithms and delta-hedgers covering shorts near PDH strike clusters drive an immediate 8-15 spot point impulse within the first 60-90 seconds. The 3-bar (15-second) confirmation filter distinguishes sustained institutional breakouts from stop-hunt spikes that reverse within one or two bars — genuine PDH breaks on NIFTY sustain above the level because the buy-side order flow exceeds remaining supply at that price. The same logic applies inversely for PDL breaks: every seller from yesterday is at a loss and fresh stop-cascades accelerate the sell-off.

indicators.name: pdh
indicators.purpose: Static level computed once per session from prior day's highs. No scaling needed — it's a prior-session anchor, not a rolling window. Valid for the entire current session.

indicators.name: pdl
indicators.purpose: Same as PDH but for the downside. These two levels bracket where all of yesterday's participants built positions.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) from 09:15 per day
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP from session open. Confirms directional bias — PDH breaks valid only when price is already above VWAP (institutional buy-side is in control of the session). No scaling because VWAP is cumulative, not windowed.

indicators.name: volume_ratio
indicators.purpose: 60-bar (5-minute) rolling volume average. Original used 20-bar 1-min SMA (same 20 minutes). Kept the same time window (5 min of 5s bars = 60 bars) because the volume baseline needs to reflect recent intraday rhythm, not the entire session. Surge on break bar signals genuine institutional participation vs. retail noise.

conditions: close[i] > pdh AND close[i-1] > pdh AND close[i-2] > pdh (3 consecutive 5s closes above PDH)
close[i-3] <= pdh (fresh break — not already above before the 3 confirmation bars)
volume_ratio[i-2] > 2.5 (volume surge on the initial break bar)
close[i] > vwap[i] (VWAP context: buy-side controlling the session)
time_minutes in [570, 780) (09:30-13:00 IST: afternoon PDH breaks have lower follow-through)
buy_ce.confirmation: Three 5-second consecutive closes above PDH (15 seconds) eliminates false spikes

conditions: close[i] < pdl AND close[i-1] < pdl AND close[i-2] < pdl (3 consecutive 5s closes below PDL)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If NIFTY reverses 8 spot points after confirming a PDH break, the institutional flow has reversed and the breakout has failed; typical false breakouts on NIFTY reverse 6-10 spot points before re-breaking.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. PDH/PDL breakouts on NIFTY produce 12-20 spot point first-leg impulses within 60-90 seconds; 7 pts captures the lower bound of this range (conservative 1:1.75 R:R ensures profitability even at 50% win rate).

filters.vix_filter: none (PDH/PDL are structural breakouts that work across VIX regimes; high VIX actually increases magnitude of PDH breaks)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-13:00 IST only — afternoon PDH breaks have lower follow-through as institutional algorithms wind down directional orders
filters.volume_filter: volume_ratio > 2.5 on break bar confirms institutional participation vs. retail probing
filters.trend_filter: VWAP directional filter ensures macro session bias aligns with breakout direction
filters.spread_filter: N/A — limit orders at close price

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — PDH/PDL are universally watched levels but volume + time + 3-bar filters add specificity. NIFTY is more efficiently priced than individual stocks, so edge is smaller but more consistent.

adaptation_notes: Original targeted NIFTY 200 stocks with 1-min bars and 30-90 min holds. Key changes: (1) Applied to NIFTY index directly — index PDH/PDL are more institutionally relevant than stock-level PDH/PDL; (2) 3-bar confirmation is now 15 seconds instead of 3 minutes — we're catching the initial breakout impulse, not waiting for trend confirmation; (3) Hold time compressed from 30-90 min to 30-90 seconds — capture the first institutional surge, not the full trend; (4) Volume baseline uses 5-min rolling (60 bars at 5s) instead of 20-bar 1-min SMA — same time window, different granularity; (5) Stops/targets converted from % of price to option premium points calibrated to 60-90s NIFTY move magnitudes.
weaknesses: NIFTY PDH/PDL breaks happen 1-3 times per day at most — very few signals, parameter sensitivity high
First day of data has no PDH/PDL — warm-up period required
Volume ratio noise at 5-second bars may cause spurious surges unrelated to institutional flow
PDH/PDL levels are the most crowded levels in NIFTY trading — break and reverse patterns are common, requiring strict confirmation
